name: browser-use
description: Real browser automation: navigate, click, type, screenshot — approval-gated.

commands.name: browse
commands.description: Open a page and work with it in the browser
commands.template: Open {input} in the browser with browser_go, take a screenshot, and complete the task with browser_click/browser_type - approval-gated.

commands.name: capture
commands.description: Capture visual evidence for a page
commands.template: Capture visual evidence for: {input}. Navigate, take a screenshot, record the URL and a short observation; do not submit a form.

commands.name: fill
commands.description: Fill a form with approval before submit
commands.template: Fill the form for: {input}. Show the exact fields and values, request approval before submit, and capture the result.

tools.name: browser_go
tools.description: Opens a headless browser and navigates to a URL. Use this tool only when you need to visually inspect a page, fill forms or interact with it. For quick web research use web_search (DuckDuckGo) instead. When you need to click buttons (e.g. cookie banners), call browser_click() afterwards. Reach: http/https and data: URLs, plus file: only inside Ephe's own output folders; other local files are read with read_file, never navigated to.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Returns an exact screenshot of the currently active headless browser. Use this when you want to look at the page (e.g. to spot cookie banners, captchas or layouts), since the image is shown to you in the chat.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Finds a described target in the headless browser via Llama-Vision and performs a mouse click on it. Required: you must have called browser_screenshot or browser_go once beforehand. Ideal for cookie banners, links or menus.

target_description.description: What exactly should be clicked (e.g. 'the big green accept button')

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Types text into the headless browser like a real keyboard. Usually executed into a search field after a preceding browser_click.

tools.name: browser_press
tools.description: Presses a single key in the headless browser (e.g. 'Enter', 'Escape').

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scrolls the current browser page in a direction by a pixel amount. Returns the new scroll position.

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluates a JavaScript expression in the current page and returns the JSON-serialized result (like Playwright page.evaluate).

tools.name: browser_exec
tools.description: Runs Python against the embedded browser with pre-imported helpers. Start the code with a one-line comment naming the step. Helpers: new_tab(url), goto_url(url), wait_for_load(), page_info(), js(expr), fill_input(selector, text), click_at_xy(x, y), capture_screenshot(), cdp(method, **params). Batch each sub-procedure into one call. Use for full page interaction in a single round-trip.

code.description: Python source using the pre-imported browser helpers; print(...) for output.

session.description: Isolated browser session name (parallel subagents use one each; omit = shared default).

timeout_s.description: Wall-clock budget for this block in seconds (1-300, default 120). On expiry the output so far is returned and the session namespace is discarded.

changelog: 1.2.0 - The browser tools ask the host. 1.1.0 - DoD pass: skill pack with two examples, commands, changelog and README entry.
